title: Escapewheel schema registry
description: Shape of logical_schemas.json, per R2 §9. Validates the registry document; column semantics are values within it, not JSON Schema types (R2 §10).

$schema.description: The meta-schema this document conforms to (R57 §2.1). Identity, not a fetch instruction -- a validator MUST NOT dereference it.

derived_from.description: Optional record of how the registry was first produced.

extension_id.description: Present on an extension registry; namespaces its tables (R17 §2).

extends.description: The logical standard version this extension was written against (R17 §5).

primary_key.description: Column names, or null for a table admitting duplicate rows (R7 §2).

since.description: The revision that introduced or last changed this, e.g. 'R8 §2' (R29 §2). A citation for a reader, not a link a validator resolves; absent means it came from 02 unamended.

type.description: R2 §4's Arrow-compatible vocabulary. Nested types are forbidden by R3 §2.1.

presence.description: R2 §5. required: present, non-null. nullable: present, may be null. optional: may be absent.

role.description: R48 §2.1. What kind of thing the column holds, which decides what a consumer may do with it -- notably whether a 1-based client converts it at the boundary (R3 §6). Closed: a consumer derives behaviour from it, so an unrecognised value would be unsafe. R55 §2.1 adds `discriminator`: the column holds a dotted resource ID naming a table, which a consumer resolves to decide what the row means.

resolves.description: R55 §2.2. Required on a discriminator, and only there. `required`: a value naming no declared resource leaves the row uninterpretable. `optional`: it is a fact -- the thing is not a packet resource.

discriminates.description: R55 §2.3.2. On a paired-value discriminator, the column holding an identifier in the named table's key space. Absent where the discriminated row shares the named table's key.

enum.description: Closed value set. A validator MUST reject values outside it.

vocabulary.description: Which vocabulary the values are drawn from (R101 §3.1). closed: the column also declares `enum` and a validator MUST reject anything outside it. open: the values name kinds of thing, comparable between packets, and a validator MUST NOT reject an unrecognised one. free: not a vocabulary at all -- a name, a description, a URI, a digest. Required on every string column but a discriminator, whose value space R55 §2.1 fixes.

reserved_values.description: Values with fixed meanings within an open vocabulary (R11 §4). Not a closed set.

since.description: The revision that introduced or last changed this, e.g. 'R8 §2' (R29 §2). A citation for a reader, not a link a validator resolves; absent means it came from 02 unamended.

determined_by.description: Columns whose values determine this one, so that rows agreeing on them agree here. An empty list declares a constant. Used to decide whether a table's sort order puts duplicate primary keys next to each other: a sort column that is determined by key columns cannot separate two rows that share a key.

identity.description: R53 §2.3. Whether an identifier's value is the source's own (`carried`) or a number this format chose (`assigned`). Not derivable -- a source may supply an integer that the writer replaces -- and it decides whether the table owes a `*_name`. Required where role is identifier, meaningless otherwise.

unit.description: R56 §2.1. The unit this column's values are in, where it does not vary. Open, as `core.sorting_runs.amplitude_unit` already is (R11 §2).

unit_from.description: R56 §2.1. The column carrying this column's unit, where it varies per row. Either a column of this table, or `resource.column` resolved through a reference this table declares -- one hop (R56 §2.3).

clock_from.description: R56 §2.2. The column holding the `clock_id` these ticks are on. Absent, the clock is the table's own `clock_id` where it has one. Coordinates only.

discriminates_via.description: Where a discriminator sits a reference away from the rows it specialises, the referencing column as `resource.column` (R90 §3.2).

positions_in.description: R100 §2.3. On a by-position discriminator, the column of this table whose value is the position column in the named resource. Absent on the other two shapes, and never beside `discriminates`.

authority.description: The nomenclatures this column's values are spelled by (R101 §3.6). Identity, not a fetch instruction: a validator MUST NOT dereference one (R14 §2.3.2) and MUST NOT reject a value for being absent from it. An array because a column's values may be drawn from more than one registry.

sql.description: Returns offending rows; empty is a pass (R2 §7.3).

advisory.description: Off by default; runs only when the caller asks (R26 §3). Never `error`, so enabling advisories cannot change whether a packet passed.
